categoryNotes.zht: 漢制，宦者掌殿省內、禁中，光祿勳領羽林等部掌殿中、殿門，衛尉巡行宮中、宮門，執金吾主宮外戒備，復有城門校尉司城門，南北軍五校尉等駐守城外。然東漢以來，執金吾漸為虛職；至魏晉，衛尉、光祿勳亦日趨閒散，宿衛之職遂輕。
categoryNotes.zhs: 汉制，宦者掌殿省内、禁中，光禄勋领羽林等部掌殿中、殿门，卫尉巡行宫中、宫门，执金吾主宫外戒备，复有城门校尉司城门，南北军五校尉等驻守城外。然东汉以来，执金吾渐为虚职；至魏晋，卫尉、光禄勋亦日趋闲散，宿卫之职遂轻。
categoryNotes.en: Under the Han system, eunuchs were responsible for guarding within the inner quarters of the palace; the Minister of the Household commanded units such as the Feathered Forest to guard the palace halls and gates; the Commandant of the Guards patrolled the palace interior and its gates; and the Bearer of the Golden Mace oversaw security outside the palace. In addition, Colonels of the City Gates were responsible for the city gates, while the Five Colonels and the Northern and Southern Armies were stationed outside the capital. From the Eastern (Later) Han onward, however, the Bearer of the Golden Mace gradually became ceremonial; by the Wei-Jin period, the Commandant of the Guards and Minister of the Household likewise became relatively unimportant, and their guard responsibilities correspondingly declined.

categoryNotes.zht: 時值三國戰亂頻仍，諸政權多擴禁衛，組建龐大「中軍」駐紮都城，以備調遣；若遣出協援州郡，則稱「外軍」。魏新立武衛、游擊等營為中軍核心，以武衛專掌宮禁；蜀則置羽林、虎步等營。魏蜀皆設五校尉，然已徒具虛名，甚而官多兵少。惟吳之宿衛，多由武衛、羽林等組成，且常以孫氏宗室統領，似猶存漢五校尉之職。
categoryNotes.zhs: 时值三国战乱频仍，诸政权多扩禁卫，组建庞大'中军'驻扎都城，以备调遣；若遣出协援州郡，则称'外军'。魏新立武卫、游击等营为中军核心，以武卫专掌宫禁；蜀则置羽林、虎步等营。魏蜀皆设五校尉，然已徒具虚名，甚至官多兵少。惟吴之宿卫，多由武卫、羽林等组成，且常以孙氏宗室统领，似犹存汉五校尉之职。
categoryNotes.en: Amid the frequent warfare of the Three Kingdoms period, the various regimes expanded their capital guards, organizing large “Central Armies” stationed near the capital for deployment; when dispatched to support local troops in the commanderies and provinces, these forces were referred to as “Outer Armies.” Wei established new units such as the Martial Guards and Mobile Forces camps as the core of its Central Army, with the Martial Guards responsible for guarding the palace. Shu also had similar units such as the Feathered Forest and Tiger Strides camps. In Wei and Shu, though the Five Colonels were established, they were largely ceremonial, and in some cases had many officers but few troops. In Wu, palace guard forces were largely drawn from units such as the Martial Guards and the Feathered Forest. These were often commanded by members of the Sun clan, and the Five Colonels there retained something closer to the functional role once fulfilled by the Han Five Colonels.

categoryNotes.zht: 洛陽城十二門，東有三門，其北曰建春門，次南曰東陽門，次南曰清明門；南有四門，其東曰開陽門，次西曰平昌門，次西曰宣陽門，次西曰津陽門；西有三門，其南曰廣陽門，次北曰西明門，次北曰閶闔門；北有二門，其東曰廣莫門，其西曰大夏門。

categoryNotes.en: Luoyang City had twelve gates. On the east side were three: to the north, Jianchun Gate; then, Dongyang Gate; and then to the south, Qingming Gate. On the south side were four: starting from the east, Kaiyang Gate, followed by Pingchang Gate, then Xuanyang Gate, and furthest west, Jinyang Gate. On the west side were three: to the south, Guangyang Gate; then, Ximing Gate; and furthest north, Changhe Gate. On the north side were two gates: to the east, Guangmo Gate, and to the west, Daxia Gate.

notes.en: In the 3rd year of Huangchu first established Commander of Provincial Forces concurrently holding the office of Inspector. Those appointed as Envoys Bearing the Imperial Tally ranked highest, followed by Bearers of the Imperial Tally, and finally Provisional Bearers of the Imperial Tally. An Envoy could execute officials of 2,000 shí rank and below. A Bearer could execute civilians and, in military campaigns, exercised the same authority as an Envoy. A Provisional Bearer could execute only those who violated military law

categoryNotes.en: All three states of Wei, Shu, and Wu established 'Comparable to Excellencies' generals such as the Grand General and General of Agile Cavalry. notes.zht: 魚豢曰：魏世驃騎車騎為都督，儀與四征同，若不為都督，雖持節屬四征者，與前後左右雜號將軍同。其或散還從文官之例，則位次三司
notes.zhs: 鱼豢曰：魏世骠骑车骑为都督，仪与四征同，若不为都督，虽持节属四征者，与前后左右杂号将军同。其或散还从文官之例，则位次三司
notes.en: Yu Huan states: In Wei, the General of Agile Cavalry and General of Chariots and Cavalry, if served as a Grand Commander, his ceremonial rank and status were equivalent to that of the Four Conquering Generals. If he did not serve as a Grand Commander, then even if he held an Imperial Tally like the Four Conquering Generals, he would only be regarded the same as Four Direction and other Miscellaneous Generals. If he was detached from military duty and returned as a civil official, he would rank just below the Three Excellencies.
